chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and a letter came to him from Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik regarding a man who dug up a woman, stripped her of her clothes, and then married her. The people have differed regarding us here; one group said, 'Kill him,' and another group said, 'Burn him.'

So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'The sanctity of the deceased is like the sanctity of the living. His Hadd is that his hand be cut off for his digging up and stripping the clothes, and the Hadd for adultery be established upon him; if he were married, he would be stoned, and if he were not married, he would be flogged with one hundred lashes.'

key_terms.أُحْصِنَ: married (specifically in the context of adultery penalties)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal penalty for a man who digs up a grave and has intercourse with the deceased?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) resolves the juristic dispute among the people of Kufa regarding the specific punishment for grave robbery by establishing that the sanctity (hurmah) of the deceased is equivalent to that of the living. He prescribes the hadd of cutting the hand for the act of digging and stripping, while separately applying the standard adultery penalties—stoning for the married (muhsan) or flogging for the unmarried—thereby distinguishing between the property violation and the sexual violation.
